test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**out**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "It was pointed _____ to her that..." is an idiomatic expression.
 
• The idiom "point out" means to inform someone of something or to draw attention to something.
 
• Therefore, "It was pointed **out** to her that..." is the correct and natural way to express that she was informed that the pavement was the place for foot passengers.
 
• The other options do not form a valid or meaningful idiom in this context.

 

Complete Passage: *That was a jolly story 1. which__ Arthur Ransome told the other day in one of his messages from Petrograd, a place in Russia. A stout old lady was walking 2. __with__ her basket down the middle of a street to the 3. __great__ confusion of the traffic and with no small peril to herself. It was pointed 4. __out__ to her that the 5. _____ was the place for the foot passengers, but she replied, “I’m going to walk where I like. We’ve got liberty now.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In: (preposition) expressing position within a space, time, or state.
 
• By: (preposition) indicating proximity, the agent of an action, or a means.
 
• So: (adverb/conjunction) indicating extent, manner, or result.
 
• Out: (adverb/preposition) indicating movement away from a place or state; often part of a phrasal verb like "point out".
